rewrite.explanation: Standard self-attention computes a score for every pair of positions, so time and memory scale with the square of the sequence length: about 10^6 pairs at 1k tokens, about 1.6 x 10^10 at 128k, and doubling the input quadruples the pair count instead of doubling it. Nothing about the training data is loaded per request, no separate model runs per output token, and no token is expanded into a document - the cost is the pairwise comparison itself. This is why long prompts get expensive faster than their length suggests, and why prompt caching, retrieval and cheaper attention variants exist.

rewrite.explanation: An RNN carries everything it has read in a single hidden state that is rewritten at every step, so information from far back has to survive many rewrites, and the gradients that would teach the model to preserve it shrink along the way; LSTMs and GRUs reduced this without removing it. Attention supplies a direct path instead: any position can draw on any earlier position in one step, whatever the distance. The quadratic pair cost belongs to attention, not to RNNs - an RNN's per-step cost is constant, which is exactly why it was cheap and forgetful.

rewrite.question: Self-attention on its own would give the same result if the input tokens were shuffled. What do positional encodings do about that?
options: Supply each token's position, so word order affects the result
Force the model to read the tokens strictly from left to right
Compress the sequence so that fewer positions have to be compared
Mark which tokens came from the user rather than from the system prompt
rewrite.explanation: Attention weights are computed from content, not from where a token sits, so without position information 'dog bites man' and 'man bites dog' would produce identical representations. Positional encodings put each position into the computation - the original transformer added position vectors to the input embeddings, while current models mostly use rotary embeddings applied inside attention, with the same purpose. Order is not the same thing as causal masking, which is what stops a position from attending to later tokens, and message roles are marked with ordinary tokens in the prompt format, not by position.
rewrite.hint: Ask what the model would need in order to tell 'dog bites man' from 'man bites dog'.
